summary: Plumas NF lookout (Butte Co.): steel station replaced a tree lookout in 1925; 55-ft steel tower built 1949; destroyed in the 2018 Camp Fire; no tower remains.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301, 1949 Revision, on a 55-foot K-brace open steel tower
facts.status_note: Destroyed in the 2018 Camp Fire (registry; FFA California-North 2018 report; Peakbagging).
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Plumas National Forest; CAL FIRE cooperator

events.note: James Hanson listed as lookout man at Big Bar (Feather River Bulletin, May 22, 1924). Earliest staffing found in the sources; the tree lookout predates it.
Forest Service supervised construction of a new steel lookout station to replace the tree lookout (Feather River Bulletin, Oct 9, 1924)
Steel lookout station replaced the old tree lookout (Plumas National Bulletin/Oroville Daily Register, Aug 1925). A May 28, 1925 report expected a 65-foot tower.
Roy Deer stationed as lookout on Big Bar Mountain (Oroville Mercury Register, Oct 8, 1928)
Constructed 1949 to California Region 5 Plan BC-301, 1949 Revision, on a 55-foot K-brace steel tower (registry). Sources do not say whether it replaced the 1925 station.
Peakbagging says not staffed since about 1976, but the same page says CAL FIRE staffs it as needed. Unresolved.
Destroyed in the Camp Fire. Registry says '2018 - Camp Fire'; FFA 2018 report confirms; Peakbagging dates it to November 2018.
Registered December 29, 2019; nominated by Brad Eells

corrections.why: The registry gives a 55-foot tower for the 1949 lookout (16.8 m). The 65-foot figure (19.8 m) describes the 1925 tower in a newspaper report.
The registry, the FFA California-North 2018 report and Peakbagging all say the lookout was destroyed in the 2018 Camp Fire. No tower stands.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Peakbagging says the lookout has not been staffed since about 1976, yet the same page says CAL FIRE staffs it as needed in fire season. Left unresolved; the 1976 event is marked as a claim from one source.
Registry gives 4,343 ft (1,324 m); Peakbagging gives 4,375 ft. The brief's 1,323.7 m matches the registry.
The 1925 tower is described as 65 feet and the 1949 tower as 55 feet. These may be different towers; the 55-foot figure is used for the tower the registry dates to 1949.

notes_for_editor: Destruction in the 2018 Camp Fire is well supported by three sources. The 1949 build date and the 1925 steel station may describe different towers; sources do not say whether the 1949 tower replaced the 1925 one. Staffing after 1928 is unresolved (Peakbagging contradicts itself). Access not recorded because no tower remains. Brief's height (19.8 m) and standing status corrected. The 1924 and 1925 newspaper items are quoted from a hobby site transcription, not the original papers.
